what: the README's headline re-measured on 0.2.3, and the model files it was measured with
setup: bin/hip-rocm101 as released in 0.2.3 (TheRock ROCm 10.2.0a20260925), the manager's profile: ctx 262144, batch/ubatch 8192, f16 K/V, -np 1, MTP with draft_max 3 and the IQ4_XS draft head, image input on. Each run on a freshly started server (tools/decode_lab.py launches one), temperature 0, seed 1, cache_prompt false, ignore_eos. The text is tmp/realtext.txt: llama.cpp's own docs, tool READMEs and src/llama-*.cpp concatenated (340,000 characters = 95,582 tokens).

model_files.check: the sha256 of each local file equals the LFS oid the Hugging Face API gives for it at this revision; sizes equal too

draft_head.check: equals the digest GitHub gives for the v0.1.2 release asset

prefill_95_6k.method: tools/decode_lab.py --model ba09dd01dc9c5fd1df9d --config dectime --words 700 --n 4 --gen 16 --gen-prefix tmp/realtext.txt --gen-prefix-chars 340000 (tmp/kvr/head_023.sh); the server's prompt eval rate

decode_86k.acceptance: 259/413 = 63%, 2.84 tokens per pass, all three runs

decode_short.method: the same without --gen-prefix: the prompt is the lab's one-line question (a B-tree explanation), 400 tokens
decode_short.acceptance: 262/394 = 66%, 2.90 tokens per pass, all three runs

reading: the first run of each decode group is a warm-up. At 86K 0.2.3 is ~2-3% slower a step than 0.2.0 (runs 2-3 30.2 ms/token against 29.4, at 2.84 against 2.80 tokens per pass); the truncation gate at 77K agrees (84.0 ms a pass against 0.2.2's 82.4); not yet traced. The decode rows moved against the 2026-09-19 ones mostly because the text did: English docs and code draft at 63% at depth where the Chinese prose of 2026-09-19 drafted at 68-69%, and the one-line question drafts at 66% where the lab's random-word probe gave 60%.
